front: How do you find the mean?
back: Add all the values, then divide by the number of values.

front: How do you find the median?
back: Put the data in order and take the middle value (or halfway between the two middle values).
The value that occurs most often. A data set can have more than one mode, or none.
Maximum − minimum. A simple measure of spread.
The median of the lower half of the ordered data.
The median of the upper half of the ordered data.

front: Finding quartiles when there is an odd number of values
back: Leave the median out of both halves, then find the median of each half.
$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$: the spread of the middle half of the data.
Minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum.

front: Why is the IQR often better than the range?
back: It ignores the top and bottom quarters, so one extreme value (outlier) hardly changes it.
